primitives.name: Confidence Gate Theorem
primitives.verbatim_quote: Theorem 2: SA monotone non-decreasing iff C2 (no inversion zones: for all a<b, E[acc | c∈[a,b]] ≤ E[acc | c≥b]); Proposition 3: C1 (pointwise rank-accuracy alignment) is a practically verifiable sufficient condition via Spearman ρ.
primitives.assumptions: Ranked decisions must satisfy C1 (rank-accuracy alignment) and C2 (no inversion zones) for monotonic improvement in accuracy upon abstention.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When confidence scores do not align with actual accuracy (C1 fails) or when accuracy decreases in higher confidence regions (C2 fails).

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's selective inference framework where confidence thresholds determine valid prediction intervals. GSE uses this to gate pick posting based on empirical validation of C1/C2.
layer2.telemetry: Spearman ρ between confidence and accuracy; inversion detection in accuracy bins.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Uncertainty decomposition Y_{x,t} = f(x) + g(x,t) + ε: *structural* uncertainty (insufficient data to estimate f — cold start; predicted from observation counts) vs *contextual* (unobserved drift g — predicted from nothing historical).

primitives.breakdown_regime: When contextual drift dominates, count-based confidence signals become unreliable; ensemble disagreement becomes necessary.

primitives.name: Adaptive Recalibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Adaptive recalibration: sliding-window re-estimation of the confidence→accuracy mapping + threshold update (fixed model).
primitives.assumptions: Confidence-accuracy mappings may shift over time and require periodic re-estimation without model retraining.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when static thresholds are applied to drifting confidence-accuracy relationships.

layer2.mapping: GSE avoids adaptive recalibration for misaligned signals; instead, it enforces C1/C2 diagnostics before deploying any gate.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal consistency of confidence thresholds; change-point detection in accuracy profiles.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Confidence Gate Theorem establishes that abstaining from ranked decisions based on confidence thresholds improves accuracy only when two conditions hold: C1 (rank-accuracy alignment) and C2 (no inversion zones). This implies that if a system’s confidence score correlates monotonically with its realized accuracy, then increasing the minimum confidence threshold will yield better overall performance. The theorem links these conditions to the structure of uncertainty: structural uncertainty arises from insufficient data (e.g., cold-start problems), while contextual uncertainty stems from unmodeled environmental drift. These uncertainties define distinct regimes where different types of confidence signals are appropriate. For instance, in sports betting, where context changes rapidly due to injuries or matchups, count-based confidence is unreliable. Instead, ensemble disagreement or recency-aware signals are preferred. Adaptive recalibration attempts to adjust thresholds over time but fails when the underlying signal is misaligned. Thus, the core insight is that deployment safety hinges on verifying C1/C2 pre-deployment rather than tuning post-hoc.
